answer.lead: Remote-approved employees can claim a one-time $500 home-office stipend, plus $50 a month toward home internet.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Remote-approved employees can claim a one-time home-office stipend of $500 toward a desk, chair, lighting or similar items for their home workspace.
The stipend is one-time: it is not repeated each year. An employee who already received the office-hybrid stipend and later becomes remote-approved can claim the difference between the two amounts. Items bought with the stipend are yours to keep.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text: Remote-approved employees can also claim $50 per month toward home internet. Office-hybrid employees cannot claim internet costs.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Office-hybrid employees can claim a one-time home-office stipend of $250 for their remote days.
Suitable items include a desk chair, a monitor arm, a desk lamp or a keyboard. The stipend can't be used for furniture unrelated to work or for general household items.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text: Remote-approved employees work remotely most of the time. The arrangement must be approved by both the manager and HR. Remote-approved employees spend at least one week per quarter at their home office.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text: Field/site-based employees, interns and contractors are not eligible for a home-office stipend.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Claim the stipend through an expense claim within 90 days of becoming eligible, with receipts. Your manager approves the claim (RSE-APR-01 §5).
You become eligible on the day your Work Arrangement starts, or on your hire date if you join with that arrangement. The internet allowance is claimed monthly as an expense, with the bill attached.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
Expense claim up to $1,000 | Manager
Expense claim $1,000.01–$5,000 | Director
Expense claim over $5,000 | VP Finance
Business-class airfare | Director
Late claim (over 60 days) | Director
Expense approvals are by the total of the claim, not by individual item. The rules behind these rows are in the Travel & Expense Reimbursement policy (RSE-EXP-01).

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
This matrix lists who approves each kind of request. "Manager" means your direct manager on the HR record. "Director" means your manager's director. "HR" means the HR Service Desk. "VP Finance" means the VP Finance, Tom Whitaker. Where a row says "none", no approval is needed, but you may still need to tell someone.
Approvals are given in the HR Portal unless a policy says otherwise. If your approver is away, their own manager can approve in their place. An approver cannot approve their own request; it goes to the next level up. The policies listed in each row hold the full rule, and this matrix only summarises who decides.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
PTO up to 10 consecutive days | Manager
PTO over 10 consecutive days | Director
Field-role PTO in the December blackout | Director
Floating holiday | Manager
Sick time | None (notify your manager)
Parental, bereavement, jury duty | HR (manager notified)
Unpaid personal leave | HR
The rules behind these rows are in the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), the Holiday Calendar & Observance policy (RSE-HOL-01) and the Leave of Absence Policy (RSE-LV-01). For example, a PTO request of 11 consecutive working days needs the director, while a request of 10 or fewer needs only the manager.

passages.title: Approval Matrix
passages.text:
Request | Approver
Temporary remote work, same state/province | None (tell your manager)
Temporary remote work, other US state/province, up to 30 calendar days/year | Manager
Temporary remote work, other US state/province, over 30 calendar days/year | HR
Working from another country (any length) | HR (Cross-Border Review)
Change to remote-approved | Manager + HR
Business travel | Manager
The rules behind these rows are in the Remote & Hybrid Work Policy (RSE-RW-01) and the Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines (RSE-LOC-01). Requests to work from another country go to HR's Cross-Border Review through an HR ticket; a manager's support is welcome but is not an approval.

Home-office stipend | Manager
Benefits changes | None (self-service in the window); HR for exceptions
